items.followUp: Prove the second equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

rubric.why: The displacement is the area under the speed-time graph, which is a trapezium.
rubric.description: Finds displacement from the trapezium area.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of acceleration to express time in terms of speeds and acceleration.
rubric.how: Accept either the acceleration formula or its rearrangement for time.

rubric.why: This follows by substituting the acceleration relation into the displacement equation and simplifying.
rubric.description: Obtains the simplified relation between displacement and speeds.

rubric.why: This is the required third equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the third equation of motion.

modelAnswer: In the speed-time graph, displacement s is equal to the area under the graph.
The area is a trapezium: s = 1/2(u + v)t.
From the definition of acceleration, a = (v − u)/t; therefore, t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting for t: s = 1/2(u + v)(v − u)/a.
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as, which is the third equation of motion.
